posts.title: LEGO Ninjago Ongoing Rumours and Discussion
posts.text: Yeah the sets descriptions almost flew under the radar for me because of how big a noise was made about the smart play news. I would give my thoughts on them but @Rolyat24 pretty much beat me to it, okay those are his thoughts but mine are pretty much the same because he makes good points. Yeah I definitely imagined more of mech to vehicle type transformation not a good to bad and I definitely agree about the listening to 'us' about a villian sets! No Frank is bad news, he needs a less ugly suit and I really hoped they'd sell us a head for him unmasked before DR ends since I can imagine that he might be relegated to the role of side character after dragon's Fury. I don't think the smart sets will impede the dragon's Fury part 2 wave too much but I do agree that it would have made more sense to apply it something like core first rather than for it into the big finale of that current era of the show. It's survived quite a lot! I'm sure it can survive this! Since it's a minifig theme they probably will be included... But as long as they don't make any character design exclusive to smart figs... ----------------------------------------------------------------------- And I've head someone's made a no-smart play in Ninjago petition, which is absurd, especially because this all leaked information! I still think it might not all be doom and gloom anyway, a smart tag isn't gonna bolster the price too much and I expect the actual smart brick will only be in one or 2 sets.

posts.title: Tips for Stop Motion Film Projects
posts.text: Definitely use clay or bluetack, if you want it to look more convincing you might have to go into post production to edit the minifigure to look like its midair. Remember to have fun too, its pretty difficult at times if you lose the spark.

posts.title: DC Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: I'll try to be objective here despite my desire that, as Constantine would say, they should clear the board, start again- as far as I can tell, it's just one reviewer who's given it a bad score and compared it to morbius. It seems like the others who have seen it generally liked it. That said, the studio sneakily dropping the reported budget 25% after the box office projections lowered is A: scummy and B: evidence that they seem to be expecting failure as well. MoT has pretty much everything riding on it, not least of which Gunn's job. Which is concerning, given the last time that a superman movie's sequel was used as a pseudo justice league movie. You throw in some other things- the purchase meaning the studio is more careful about what they're approving, Supergirl's actress scrubbing all her instagram posts about her role as supergirl, etc- taken seperately none of these things are all that concerning but put together, I may have been right when I said the interval between batman movies could outlast the entire DCU. All it'd take is the Gorilla Grodd show releasing first and that Nightwing/Red Hood street urchins movie rightfully getting cancelled. And of course, by saying that I have now confirmed that the one guy's morbius comparison was an outlier and Clayface is actually going to do so well a sequel is immediately greenlit. You're welcome, DCU fans.

posts.title: Marvel Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: I think everyone's sort of expecting it but the leakers say that internally marvel is still acting as if they can hit the december 2027 release date, so unless that changes soon I imagine either we get the secret wars sets in october or there's a secret wars shaped gap in the lineup. They're 100% working on them right now- we've had the leaked price points for a little while and the release date is less than a year out. I could buy that there's some crunch for new tie-ins compared to the normal 1.5 year development cycle, but not THAT much- something like the NWH spoiler set you'd imagine they would be trying to get out as fast as possible, and that one took 1.5 years almost to the day. I still want to know about this second wave of doomsday sets since even though leakers have seemingly confirmed it, I'm worried it's some sort of mirage. How do we know 1HY and then have price points for the secret wars sets, but not the pricepoints that could correspond to the Doomsday wave 2 sets? I'm sure they clash in the movie but it's hilarious that immediately following TFATWS the next time we see Sam he's working directly with the US president. "No, John, you can't work for the UN to hunt down the super-terrorists - Oh, hello, Mr President who's hulk's mortal enemy and helped split up the avengers while I was on the team, I'd love to meet with you and attend your victory speech."

posts.title: Davejsp's Technic Creations
posts.text: <- Back to Index of Davejsp's Technic MOCs thread 42099 Wild Beast This is one of my B-Models for the LEGO Techncic set 42099 4x4 X-treme Off-Roader. This "Wild Beast" MOC has a gear ratio of 1:1.67 and I bet you're asking if it can run at all, like, it shouldn't have enough torque to drag its weight around... Chapter 1: Planning for speed Things I knew from the start that had to be implemented: -Using the set's planetary wheels hub was out of the question. -To reach a gear ratio higher than 1:1, gears had to be used. The MOC needed to be RWD only and the two XL motors dedicated to the two rear wheels with the transmission being as simple and short as possible to avoid friction, and the gears couldn't be in a perpendicular setup to avoid loss of efficiency. -If the MOC was going to be fast, I would need to steer with precision, to help with that, I wanted the front axle to have a positive caster angle. -Being fast means it also needs a sturdy chassis, so, for this MOC in particular, I would be using as many pieces as necessary to make the chassis as robust as possible and make it impossible for the structure to disassemble while running. -Some kind of suspension was necessary, but at this point, I still wasn't sure what direction I would take; I didn't want to use independent suspension on all wheels to avoid complexity (and possibly more friction) though, but something simpler. Chapter 2: Chassis When it comes to RC MOCs, I almost always start by designing the chassis and making the electric components an integral part of it. Since this would be an original MOC and not a replica of anything, I was free to do whatever I wanted, in the end, I just wanted something with an aerodynamic aesthetic. Rear axle I started with the rear axle, using the set's differential was not an option because it would require gears in a perpendicular setup and it's just not efficient; I took some time to decide between having both XL motors driving a solid axle, or the two XL motors driving one rear wheel each, independently, I went with the second option mostly because a solid axle would create a lot of stress when steering and slow down the MOC a lot. Then it went through several redesigns because the prototype rear axle was too wide, I ended up using a solid structure with an unconventional, asymmetric design for the rear axle. Front axle Before starting to design the front axle, I had to decide what kind of suspension the MOC would have. Since I wanted to focus on steering precision and the rear axle was a solid structure, I decided to implement live axle suspension on the rear axle only. Without suspension at the front, the build required much less complexity, this allowed me to create a very simple and solid front axle, with a positive caster angle, which helps the steering align naturally on its own. Chassis The next step was to connect both the front axle and rear axle to a center structure containing the hub and test the hell out of it for sturdiness; a turntable was used to implement the live axle suspension at the rear. Then I created a profile on the Powered Up app and drove the chassis around like crazy, oh man, was it fast... I wish I had some footage of that. Chapter 3: Modelling Now that I have a functioning chassis, I need to give it shape, as I mentioned before, I didn't have a specific idea, I just wanted something aerodynamic, probably some kind of buggy, so I started experimenting with the set's panels. It didn't take much time for me to start forming an overall shape in my head and start working towards it. I started with the front, aggressive-looking headlights, and low profile; and built the dash and basic interior; for the rear bodywork, I tried to make it look somehow curvy to be consistent with the rest of the design. The rear axle has a lot of travel because of the live axle suspension, so I couldn't build a very solid structure for the rear end, it's basically just a suspended platform for the tail lights and exhaust, it

posts.title: Marvel Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: That's pretty much the premise of The Marvels: "Carol's a bad friend, family member, and even enemy and needs to mend her ways." It comes off more like the writers, through Monica and others, berating her for not fitting their preferred mould of "overtly emotional female character obsessed with motherhood" while desperately dressing her up in girly frills (all the singing, dancing, and romancing a prince - she even somehow changes her Starforcer suit into a dress for that!). There's some other stuff as well in this supposedly feminist Marvel movie (admittedly an oxymoron). Like Fury lording it over all three of our heroines (the same Fury that was little more than Carol's sidekick in her first movie, and who has made one catastrophic mistake of his own after the other since then, not to mention harvesting Carol's DNA without permission and making it available to terrorists, thought at least The Marvels blatantly ignores all the Secret Invasion stuff). Or that one guy on the water planet ordering Monica to smile more which she immediately does. Or the female villain being an overtly emotional mess who backstabs people at a time when it brings her absolutely no benefit because, y'all know, women are irrational. Frankly Brie Larson should have gotten another Oscar for somehow selling all of this (the fact that I still like Carol and would love to see more of her is a testament to her acting skills). And the really sad thing is that The Marvels still isn't the worst movie the MCU have brought out in phase 4-6, not even by a long shot. (It even has what I would consider THE best scene in all the MCU movies, set to the soundtrack of "Memory". But that's wholly unrelated to its, and the MCU as a whole's, treatment of female characters.) I should have been clearer about that, sorry. Carol's reckless and angry (she's not the original Avenger for nothing ;-)) which, yes, are emotions. But she's not a typical MCU heroine who constantly worries about how her friends and family see her or who'd burn the world solely for her family. Carol's a "get the job done" person and while she often acts before thinking, again she does so because she's being provoked into anger. In that way she's akin to many masculine heroes. This worked perfectly fine in the first movie. However in The Marvels her lack of attachment to concepts like family - and again she WAS there for Maria and Monica even during a galaxy-wide crisis as much as she could, it's just that she wouldn't neglect her job and drop everything for them when that's what the writers expect from a "good" female character - is suddenly a problem. The movie ends with her "redeeming herself" by moving to Earth in order to play caretaker for Monica's empty house and I guess sometimes hang out with Kamala, effectively giving up her job for no good reason (but finally fitting into the "family always comes first" mould the writers prefer).

posts.title: Marvel Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: Again I agree with the premise, just not that it was poor handling. They're angry and revenge filled in the immediate aftermath, yes, because a guy just killed half of all living things. But most of them aren't consumed by it- the early scenes post timeskip do a good job showing that. Cap and Widow can't move on, but they're not boiling with vengeance, they're trying to help other people get past it. Tony started a family and initially doesn't even want to try to bring everyone back. Clint is the only one who became consumed by vengeance, but it's comic-accurate and also makes sense for the character- he was the family man of the avengers, he got out, he retired, and then they all died in an event he wasn't even aware was happening until it was too late. I would say hulk and thor weren't handled as well, but Hulk's issues arguably stem from the fact that he should have been angrier instead of dabbing with adoring fans, and Thor... I mean, I think they were going for depression there? It definitely didn't work but I didn't get the sense he was filled with rage as much as sorrow. Beautifully written explanation of John's character, much better than I could have said it. The scene of him, after losing everything, welding that makeshift shield together in the garage is something that gets to the spirit of Cap and a Captain America legacy character more than anything Sam (or Bucky in any of the comics I read in his time as cap) have ever done. Back when the show first came out I thought it should have ended with them deciding that no one man can live up to steve rogers, and having Sam, Bucky, and John all carry on his legacy with none of them being specifically captain america. (Namewise you could keep USAgent, though I dislike the name so I'd rather go with his original comics pre-cap name of Patriot. Winter Soldier is fine too since it's already a reference to the American Revolution, and while Sam is the trickiest I think there's definitely something there either with an Eagle motif or just keeping Falcon) I think they've really been pushing an attempt to do a similar thing to that by constantly bringing up that Sam doesn't have serum, but it falls flat in two ways. The first is that his projects practically treat him as if he has the serum anyway in combat, and the second is that in the middle of his show the wakandans- who Sam doesn't really even have any connection to- just show up and given him a suit made of the same metal as his shield. If anything he has MORE raw power than Steve did while in the suit, not to mention he can fly and use the black panther kinetic shield blast. And of course, he's always treated as 100% in the right and with bucky/the wakandans/etc hyping him up. The writers want you to root for him as if he's an underdog but don't put any work into making him one. Also important to point out that Sam and Bucky - and to be fair to Sam, he does push back on this... a little bit....- were already talking about beating the tar out of John and stealing the shield before he kills the flag smasher. Which is a huge writing misstep, because it really just exacerbates their fight with John looking less like them taking the shield back from someone unworthy and more like two guys- one of them ostensibly a veteran counselor- taking advantage of a veteran's panic attack to jump him.

posts.title: Modular Building Sets - Rumours and Discussion
posts.text: They have done at least some green space elements. The Spring Lantern Festival was the only one in the CNY series to be on a baseplate and be modular compatible. I think specifically because it could be included as a park. The Ideas Botanical Gardens is also very modular compatible. But the thing with parks is that you don't get a huge amount for the cost, so it's a harder value proposition than a building. Look at the Gardens of the World series, which are generally seen as being far too expensive. Admittedly, a lot of them is about the base, which doesn't add a huge amount of value, but it does give the option to swap things around and customize. And then you look at the trees in things like the Ideas Treehouse, A-frame cabin, and The Shire, which are all pretty terrible, as they're too sparse. But having built MOC upgrades of them, it adds SO MANY MORE PARTS to make the trees look decent, and it's not really a mass market build experience that will be enjoyable for most. So I can see why they don't do more green spaces, even though I would like them too. But Rebrickable is a great source.
